chunk_findings.detail:
The holder note survives a crashed holder, because it is only removed in the `finally` of a live
process and the `with contextlib.suppress(OSError)` swallows any failure — yet the flock it
describes is released by the kernel when the holder dies. `_holders` then reads notes for *all*
indices `0..limit-1`, held or not, and `min(..., key=at)` deliberately prefers the *oldest* note,
i.e. exactly the stale one. Concrete case with `ci.max_concurrent_suites = 2`: run A takes slot 0
at 09:00 and is SIGKILLed at 09:05 (leaving `suites.0.holder`, slot now free), run B takes slot 1
at 10:00, run C starts at 10:01 and times out after `suite_wait_s`. `_holders` returns A's note
(older `at`) and the refused run reports "blocked on <A> since 09:00:00" even though A is gone and
the actual live blocker is B. The docstring's invariant ("they are only read while the slot is
held") is therefore false, and the message — the sole purpose of the note — is systematically
wrong after any crash. Fix by clearing/ignoring notes for unheld slots (or by keying the message
off which slots are currently locked rather than off file age).

chunk_findings.detail: The test plants a stale note at index 0 and then takes two holds with `limit=2`, but slot acquisition starts at the lowest free index, so the very first `with SL.hold(cfg(limit=2), "agent-b", tmp_path)` acquires slot 0 and overwrites the planted `{"holder": "dead", "at": 1, ...}` note. By the time the third `hold(...)` raises `SuiteBusy`, the only notes left in slots `0..limit-1` are the two *live* ones (`agent-b` at slot 0, `agent-c` at slot 1), so a `_holders` that blindly reads all note files (the unfixed behaviour, which preferred the oldest `at`) now returns `agent-b` — exactly what the assertion accepts. The test therefore passes unchanged on the unfixed code and does not satisfy the stated requirement that the regression test FAIL before the fix; to make it discriminating, the planted note must live at an index the two live holds do not reuse (e.g. `limit=3` with the stale note at index 2), so that the stale entry survives into the `_holders` call.
